summary_md: Two processes: **the pet feeder** (`python -m gamelab pet --every 1 --map 10002073`), one Python process that keeps her pet fed and runs **the guard** that parks her when she's in trouble between hunts, and **the babysitter** (`D:/MapleHelper-scratch/live/babysit3.ps1`, a PowerShell loop outside the repo) that starts the pet feeder whenever no hunt runs and kills it within 5 s of one starting. Almost everything in the pet feeder runs one step after another on its main thread (the feeding, the guard, the potion and death alerts). A few helper threads carry the pipe to the perception service, the telemetry file, a once-a-minute garbage-collection report and the phone pushes (and four name-tag search threads during a Character Info read). The park and a missing perception service are started through a short `powershell.exe` child that asks WMI to start them, so they are not the pet feeder's children and outlive it.

processes.plain_md:
**The pet feeder** is a standalone Windows process: its own `python.exe`, **not** elevated, with no window. The babysitter starts it hidden and appends its console to `D:/MapleHelper-scratch/live/pet.log`.

**You are not expected to start it.** The babysitter starts `python -m gamelab pet --every 1 --map 10002073` within 5 s whenever no hunting command runs (a `nav --park` counts as one), and again within 5 s whenever it ends by itself. It kills it (a hard kill: nothing in it runs at its end) within 5 s of a hunt starting, because a hunt feeds the pet itself. Nothing in gamelab keeps it to one copy; the babysitter's process list does.

**What it does.** Once a minute it brings the pet's fullness up to date (one point lost every 55 s while the game window is up) and, under 60, asks the elevated key player to tap the pet food key: about one food every 27.5 minutes. Only when the number isn't known does it double-click her to read it off her Character Info. For the next 60 s **the guard** runs, a pass a second: from the perception service's newest state it watches for touches, low HP, potions running out and death, pushes to your phone, and starts a separate `nav --park --tell` process that walks her to a safe place. It never captures the screen (it asks the perception service for frames) and presses keys only through the player; it keeps feeding through a Lie Detector.

**How it ends.** It runs until it is killed (by the babysitter, or Ctrl+C if you ran it in a terminal). It ends by itself with exit 0 when the game's client switches to another calibrated size (so the babysitter starts one with eyes for that size), or with exit 1 when an error escapes its loop, such as a frame the service can't give in the middle of a Character Info read.

`pet` without `--every` (one follow, then it ends) and `pet --read` (read the fullness now) are one-off runs for you or Claude in a terminal. The hunt's checks (key bindings, stat window, chat box) and its attack model (`behavior/presence.py`) never run in it.
processes.expected_start: the babysitter, automatically: it starts `pet --every 1 --map 10002073` within 5 s whenever no hunting command (nor a park) runs, so again after every hunt or park, and again after it ends by itself; you or Claude by hand only for a one-off `pet` or `pet --read` in a terminal

components.runs_as: library code on the caller's thread (the main thread)
components.started_by: the Hunter's Actions, built at start-up
components.lives: as long as the process
components.does: Every key and click the pet feeder sends is a small JSON plan written into `gamelab/lab/inbox` and played by the elevated key player (`python -m gamelab player`), the only process whose input reaches the game; it waits for the answer in `gamelab/lab/outbox` (looked for every 10 ms, 120 s at most). A food is one tap of the pet food key with kind `pet_food`, which the player takes even with the Lie Detector alarm up (a few a minute). The plans ask for focus, so the player brings the game to the front first if another window is in front (never while the alarm is up). Before each follow it rereads her remembered key bindings (`gamelab/lab/keybindings-<her>.json`), follows any change and rewrites `gamelab/lab/alarm_keys.json` for the player. With no player running, the plan waits its 120 s unanswered, is withdrawn, and the food is tried again next round (no guard passes during that wait).

components.name: The guard
components.runs_as: library code on the caller's thread (the main thread, inside `_guarded` between follows)
components.started_by: `_guard_pass`, built at start-up (only with `--every`)
components.lives: as long as the process; its episode state is kept in `gamelab/lab/guard.json` across restarts
components.does: Once a second (`Pass.tick`): reads its switch (`gamelab/lab/guard_mode.txt`, set by `gamelab guard off|alert|on`; on when there's no file), turns a hunt that died without parking (`gamelab/lab/hunt.json` whose process is gone) into a note (`gamelab/lab/park_note.json`), and takes the perception service's newest state if it is under 3 s old (no waiting, no asking for a frame). Two touches on her within 30 s, her HP under the stop rule on two passes in a row (unless she's known parked), or a note set it off. Then, in order: a hunt running, nothing (the babysitter is about to kill this process); dead, nothing; Lie Detector alarm up, no moves; someone playing by hand (Windows' last input later than the player's last key, with the game in front), left alone; switch on `alert`, one "She needs you" push and no moves; the game in front and the player running, it starts a park (at most every 2 minutes, 3 times an episode) and pushes "Parking her"; otherwise one push saying why not, and she parks once the game is back. It never brings the game forward or starts the player. After 5 minutes with no usable state (the game behind another window or minimized, or her on another map than `--map`), one "The guard can't see her" push unless she's known parked. The README marks the guard as not yet tried live, and on 2026-11-16 `guard_mode.txt` said `alert`: pushes, no parks.

components.name: The perception service's client (`perceive-client` thread)
components.runs_as: thread
components.started_by: `_perception` at start-up (ServiceClient.start)
components.lives: as long as the process (a daemon thread)
components.does: Connects to the perception service's named pipe `\\.\pipe\gamelab-perceive` (its key read from `gamelab/lab/perceive.json`) and says hello as `pet`: a command that sends keys but doesn't hunt. So the service never refuses it and never lets it hold the map: with no hunt attached it has the service look at the pet's `--map`, and a hunt on another map takes the service over. From then on it receives every state the service makes (the service runs at one pace, 15 frames a second, whoever is attached) and the answers to whole-frame asks, whose pixels come through shared memory; it keeps the last 8 states. It reconnects every 0.5 s if the pipe closes or says nothing for 10 s, and while it can't reach a service it starts one.

processes.plain_md:
**The babysitter** is not in the repo. It is the PowerShell script `D:/MapleHelper-scratch/live/babysit3.ps1`, running as its own `powershell.exe`, not elevated (nothing in it asks for administrator rights). The same folder keeps `babysit.ps1` and `babysit2.ps1` for rollback; the project's notes say babysit3 has been the live one since 2026-10-26. The README still names `babysit.ps1` in places, and `D:/MapleHelper-scratch/pconst/finish/babysit3.ps1`, a folder that no longer exists.

**What it does.** Every 5 s it lists the python processes and keeps things running: one `gamelab perceive --map 10002073` always, the rolling recording handed over to it, and the pet feeder (`gamelab pet --every 1 --map 10002073`) exactly while no `gamelab tour|hunt|nav|probe|combo|act|do` process runs. It also drops simulator and test pythons to Idle priority. It starts everything through WMI (hidden, in D:/MapleHelper, with `C:/Users/Admin/.conda/envs/maplehelper/python.exe`, a junction to `D:/conda-envs/maplehelper314`), so what it starts is not its child and outlives it. It stops things with a hard kill.

**Who starts it: you or Claude, by hand, once.** Its header and the README say to start it detached through WMI (`Invoke-CimMethod Win32_Process Create ... powershell.exe -File D:/MapleHelper-scratch/live/babysit3.ps1`) so it outlives the Claude Code session. Nothing that starts it again was found: no scheduled-task file, startup script or Claude loop in D:/MapleHelper-scratch or C:/Users/Admin/.claude names it (Windows' own scheduled-task list wasn't read). The notes only say to check it is alive after restarts.

**How long it lives.** Until its powershell is killed or the PC restarts; an error in one round is logged and the loop goes on. It doesn't look like it has run lately: its logs (`babysit.log`, `pet.log`, `perceive.log`) are not in `D:/MapleHelper-scratch/live/`, and `gamelab/lab/pet.json`, which a running pet feeder rewrites every minute, was last written on 2026-11-07.
processes.expected_start: you or Claude, by hand, once per PC session: detached through WMI (`Invoke-CimMethod -ClassName Win32_Process -MethodName Create`, `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File D:/MapleHelper-scratch/live/babysit3.ps1`, folder D:/MapleHelper); nothing found restarts it automatically
